source.author: ov
source.text: Ergo, ne quicquam mundus Iove maius haberet, quamvis haud tepidos sub pectore senserat ignes, Iuppiter aequoreae Thetidis conubia fugit in suaque Aeaciden succedere vota nepotem iussit et amplexus in virginis ire marinae.
source.text_original: Ergo, ne quicquam mundus Iove maius haberet, / quamvis haud tepidos sub pectore senserat ignes, / Iuppiter aequoreae Thetidis conubia fugit / in suaque Aeaciden succedere vota nepotem / iussit et amplexus in virginis ire marinae.
source.text_english: Therefore, lest the world should have anything greater than Iove, although he had felt fires not cold under his breast, Iuppiter fled the marriage bed of sea-born Thetis and ordered Aeacides his grandson to take his place in his own stead, and to go into the embrace of the sea-maiden virgin.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: Tyrrheni tergore piscis Peleos in thalamos vehitur Thetis; aequora delphin corripit, illa sedet deiecta in lumina palla nec love maiorem nasci suspirat Achillen.
reuse.text_original: Tyrrheni tergore piscis / Peleos in thalamos vehitur Thetis; aequora delphin / corripit, illa sedet deiecta in lumina palla / nec love maiorem nasci suspirat Achillen.
reuse.text_english: Peleus is borne to the bridal chambers by Thetis, a Tyrrhenian fish, on its back; the dolphin speeds over the seas. She sits with her cloak fallen over her eyes and does not sigh that Achilles is born, greater than Jupiter.
